title_en: Nuh's son who would not board
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: While the ship ran with them through waves like mountains, Nuh called to his son, who was standing apart, and told him to come aboard with them and not to be with the disbelievers.
The son answered that he would take refuge on a mountain that would protect him from the water.
The reply was that today there is no protector from the command of God, except for the one on whom He has mercy.
The waves came between them, and the son was among the drowned.

chapters.summary_md: Nuh called to his son and told him to come aboard and not be with the disbelievers [c1]. The son answered that a mountain would protect him from the water, but the waves came between them and he was among the drowned [c2][c4].
chapters.body_md: While the ship ran with them through waves like mountains, Nuh called to his son, who was standing apart, and told him to come aboard with them and not to be with the disbelievers [c1]. The son answered that he would take refuge on a mountain that would protect him from the water [c2]. The reply was that today there is no protector from the command of God, except for the one on whom He has mercy [c3]. The waves came between them, and the son was among the drowned [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah gives the son's answer and then a reply that no one is protected from God's command except those on whom He has mercy [c3]. It does not say who gave that reply, although it follows Nuh's call [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Nuh called to his son to come aboard the ship [c1]. The son said a mountain would keep him safe [c2]. Then the waves came between them [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage places safety in God's mercy and not in anything else [c3]. Another is that the call to come aboard was an invitation that the son did not accept [c1][c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the name or age of the son, or whether he had heard Nuh's call before this moment.
- The ayah says only that it ran; the ship is named in the previous ayah (11:41), which lies outside the verses of this item.
- Not established: who spoke the reply about the command of God; the ayah does not mark the speaker.
- Not established: where the mountain was, or whether the son reached it.

claims.statement_en: The earth was told to swallow its water and the sky to hold back, the water subsided, the matter was decided, and the ship came to rest on the Judi.
The ayah adds a word of rejection for the wrongdoing people.
Nuh called to his Lord and said that his son was of his family, that God's promise is true, and that God is the most just of judges.

God told Nuh that the son was not of his family, describing him with the words an unrighteous deed, and told him not to ask Him about what he had no knowledge of, warning him not to be among the ignorant.
Nuh answered that he sought refuge in God from asking about what he had no knowledge of, and that unless God forgave him and had mercy on him, he would be among the losers.

chapters.summary_md: Nuh called to his Lord that his son was of his family and that God's promise is true [c3]. God told him that the son was not of his family and told him not to ask about what he had no knowledge of [c4]. Nuh sought refuge in God from such asking and asked for forgiveness and mercy [c5].
chapters.body_md: The earth was told to swallow its water and the sky to hold back, the water subsided, the matter was decided, and the ship came to rest on the Judi [c1]. The ayah adds a word of rejection for the wrongdoing people [c2]. Nuh called to his Lord and said that his son was of his family, that God's promise is true, and that God is the most just of judges [c3]. God told Nuh that the son was not of his family, describing him with the words an unrighteous deed, and told him not to ask Him about what he had no knowledge of, warning him not to be among the ignorant [c4]. Nuh answered that he sought refuge in God from asking about what he had no knowledge of, and that unless God forgave him and had mercy on him, he would be among the losers [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The words describing the son as an unrighteous deed can be read as saying that he was an unrighteous deed or that his deed was unrighteous, and the ayah is brief [c4]. The ayat do not explain the words not of your family any further [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The water went down and the ship came to rest [c1]. Nuh asked his Lord about his son [c3]. God told Nuh not to ask about what he did not know [c4]. Nuh asked God to forgive him and to have mercy on him [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Nuh, when corrected, sought refuge in God and asked for forgiveness [c4][c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the words not of your family mean in detail; readers differ on whether they speak of kinship, of belief or of conduct.
- Not established: whether Nuh was asking for his son's rescue, for forgiveness for him, or for something else; the ayah says only that his son was of his family and that God's promise is true.
- Not established: what the matter was that was decided, or how many were aboard the ship.
- Not established: where the Judi is.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the son is called Kanaan or Yam, and later works add details of his age and conduct.
The ayat do not say whether the son was a believer at any time, and the meaning of not of your family is read in different ways.
Hadith to add later: reports about Nuh's son and the passage 11:45-47, with a named grader for each; none is used here.
